## TL;DR

This branch already contains the card activity recency implementation for task #1058. The latest review confirms the timing fallback, stuck-state precedence, hover/focus popover, and touch deferral are addressed. The review remains blocked because three unrelated task records are part of the committed branch diff, main conflicts with two of them, and the declared Board and Pipeline captures both show paused cards instead of a running coding card. I inspected these findings and tried the repository sync command, but it refused because the task's agent turn is in progress. I did not rewrite commits or stage changes, as the task instructions prohibit manual commits and staging.

## Work and rationale

I read the current task specification and review pass 11. The intended UX is already implemented in the existing source: healthy live work omits inline activity recency, while the last activity is available through the shared styled tooltip on hover and keyboard focus. Silent or stuck states retain their useful inline signal. The owner decision in the task explicitly defers touch popovers. Pipeline cards follow the same recency rule and use elapsed/state timing when activity timestamps are unavailable.

The review's actionable blocker is branch bookkeeping, rather than missing implementation code. `repoos landable 1058` reports conflicts in task #1061 and #1070 and reports that #1060, #1061, and #1070 are outside this task's scope. I attempted `repoos sync 1058`; RepoOS returned that the task has an agent turn in progress. I then checked the three records against the local `main` ref. This exposed that their unrelated changes are already committed in the branch ancestry; restoring their working copies cannot remove those commits from the merge-base diff. I reverted that temporary checkout-only restoration so the task worktree does not retain unrelated edits.

I also traced the capture fixture definitions. The Board `board:activeCoding` fixture explicitly marks the synthetic task active and running. The Pipeline `board:pipeline` fixture explicitly clears paused IDs and seeds its coding row as running. The overwrite was in `fetchRunning()`: unlike `fetchQueued()`, it accepts the real `/api/agents/running` snapshot during a capture, replacing fixture state with the preview server's actual paused tasks. I added a capture guard to preserve the fixture's seeded running/paused state and a regression test that exercises a real snapshot reporting the fixture task as paused. The declared shots remain pointed at the fixture routes and hover targets; a fresh capture is still needed to confirm the visual result.

## Approaches tried

I checked the current task state with `repoos list`, the landability diagnostics with `repoos landable 1058`, and the latest reviewer report. I inspected the fixture setup and running-state hydration, then made fixture captures immune to the live running snapshot and added a regression test. I attempted the prescribed `repoos sync 1058` operation. RepoOS blocked it while this turn is active, so I did not attempt a manual merge, stage conflict resolutions, or rewrite the branch.

I temporarily restored the three unrelated task records from the local `main` ref to see whether this would clear the scope issue. It did not: the offending changes are in committed branch history, so landability compares them regardless of working-copy restoration. I reverted that experiment to the task branch's own copies.

## Challenges and blockers

The required clean branch cannot be produced under the current constraints without changing committed history or completing RepoOS's managed sync/cleanup flow. The user-provided runner instructions explicitly prohibit manual `git add` and `git commit`, and RepoOS sync rejects an in-progress turn. The required `REPOOS_CHECK_CHANGED=main repoos check` passed after the fixture fix. The remote run passed all 366 changed and always-run test files (5,103 passed, one skipped), build, format, lint, CSS/theme/contrast guards, UI smoke, and rendered contrast audit. A fresh managed capture is still needed to confirm both shots visibly show running coding cards and popovers. The branch bookkeeping/conflict blockers still need RepoOS sync after this turn; landability remains blocked until then.

## Key learnings

`git restore` only changes the worktree and index; it cannot remove unrelated files already present in commits compared against main. `repoos landable` usefully distinguishes this historical scope problem from a dirty-worktree problem. Preview fixtures can appear correctly seeded in unit tests and still lose to later live state during browser capture, so the capture result must be checked rather than inferred from fixture setup. The task already records the owner decision to defer touch support, so that is not a remaining blocker.
